steps.claim: Expected-program compatibility requires the same ordered interface roles, widths/classes, region shapes/roles, classical parameter types and ordered checked borrowed-bundle widths/classes. Components correspond by interface slot and checked lifetime position. Internal action loop bounds describe the body and its identity, rather than an additional interface component.

steps.claim: replay09 checks only p.signature() != f.signature(). That includes internal bounds but omits borrowed lifetime requirements. It then executes the expected program with the subject's same Invocation, whose borrowed_widths came only from f; execute_element_bound uses that inventory even when f is the expected function.

In fixed-image-incompatible.bisa, lookup is the unchanged controlled-dirty subject with inventory [1]. Added clean has the identical signature and qload/cx/qunload body but no qborrow or cancelling borrowed CX pair, hence inventory []. The claim expects clean at args=[], budget=[0,0,0,0], fixed image 0102 and one inherited control. Parse and check_hashes succeed, and both checker APIs incorrectly return ProofRelativeToImage with n=256, |D|=16777216 and fraction=1/65536. The required outcome is rejection for incompatible borrowed interfaces. The smaller incompatible-empty.bisa likewise returns unrestricted Proof for [1] versus [], and incompatible-narrower.bisa returns Proof for [2] versus [1].

Conversely, compatible-different-bounds.bisa compares a(t)={qloop 2 {x t; x t}} with z(t)={x t; x t}. Both have one mutable bit, no other slots/arguments/borrows and identity semantics. The full t=0..1 domain with args=[] and zero budget must give Proof, n=|D|=2. Both APIs instead reject with 'expected program has an incompatible signature' because bounds [2] differs from [].

The compatibility predicate is simultaneously too weak for borrowed interfaces and too strict for legal source bodies. The fixed-image proof in step <1>3 is issued for a relation that fails the mandated interface precondition, while step <1>4 rejects a legal relation. These are S0 divergences, not an optional implementation restriction or an ambiguity.

sol.problem: K73 compatibility is approximated by full signature equality. Subject-only borrowed inventory is then reused for the expected program, allowing a missing/narrower expected lifetime to be padded silently. At the same time, different internal loop bounds cause a false incompatibility rejection. The fixed-image witness is directly on the K85 program-relation path. Both behaviors also reproduce against a0b49a0, so this is a newly reproduced existing defect, not a regression introduced by the four fix commits.
sol.fix: Change reference-interpreter/src/claims/replay09.rs::replay09 to compare a shared K73 interface descriptor, using Object::checked_borrow_lifetimes independently for the subject and expected closure. §12.1 K73 requires 'the same ordered interface roles' and 'ordered borrowed-bundle widths/classes as the subject'; compare the specified bundle/region/argument and checked-lifetime components in order, including applicable class bindings, without treating body loop bounds as an interface mismatch. Obtain the expected program's own checked inventory before constructing its replay context; a known count/width mismatch rejects, and unavailable/host-limited inventory must never be guessed from the subject or establish a successful verdict. Add tests in tests/isa09_fixed_image.rs: (1) copy controlled-dirty's function to @clean, remove b=qborrow any 1, both cx b t rows and qreturn b, rehash the new object, and set expected.program to clean; with the original complete domain/image/control/invocation, both APIs must reject for K73 incompatibility (currently both return ProofRelativeToImage); (2) same-shape one-bit identity actions qloop 2 {x t; x t} and x t; x t, no borrows, full t range, args=[], budget=[0,0,0,0], must return Proof with n=2, |D|=2 and fraction=1/1 (currently both reject); (3) subject qborrow width 2 versus expected width 1 must reject even though the larger subject pool can execute both. Retain positive equal-inventory program comparisons, renamed interface correspondence, omitted-lifetime evidence and all existing table regressions.
